proof_scope: In progress. R1774 assembles the exact symmetric complex average from the forward and inverse Mobius actions. The transport constant is bounded by one fixed constant when |g00| and |g10| are at most two; controlling |g11| also supplies the inverse bound. Thus upper and lower distant-band sums decay as 2^(-D) with a constant independent of the input, truncations, number of generators and generator choice within this bounded class. A finite symmetric-matrix reindexing and the shifted band-energy estimate control the near part. If every band has norm ratio at most r, the finite quadratic correlation is at most 2*(D*r*B0 + 2^(-D)*L)*||f||^2. Choosing universal D and r>0 makes this less than 1/3 for unit inputs. Hence a finite band sum with correlation at least 1/3 implies that the full decomposition has some nonzero band u_j with ||T u_j||>r*||u_j||; no bound j<N is asserted. The grid-input corollary uses the verified R1773 eventual finite correlation. This is currently a level-zero decomposition, not the arbitrary-high-start version needed later.

Prove the exact tail reconstruction sum_(j<N) u_(J+j)=v_(J+N)-v_J, where v_J=F_inverse(rho_J*Ff), and its L2 limit f-v_J. The existing sharp-low grid estimate with R=2^(J+1) gives distance at most 1/16 when K^2>=16384*pi^2*2^(3J). Retain correlation and extend the offset argument using shifted finite index sets; the existing far theorem already accepts arbitrary sets, so do not introduce a constant that grows with J. The current J=0 result must not be described as the full arbitrary-k0 source Claim 3.3.

Then address the selected band's relative moments before importing the perturbation step in Claim 3.4. A concrete route is joint selection: form a nonnegative cost M_j from ||x^m u_j||^2 and 2^(-2j)||x^m u_j'||^2 for m=0,1,2; prove its summed bound from the existing cutoff estimates. Declare a band good when M_j<=R*||u_j||^2. Bad bands have small total squared norm for fixed sufficiently large R. Prove that the L2 norm of their sum is controlled by that energy using the bounded Fourier overlap, retain a positive correlation on the good-band sum, then isolate within that set. This is a proposed route, not a proved joint-selection theorem. Check the needed matrix-parameter perturbation estimate explicitly rather than assuming frequency localization gives spatial support or uniform moments.
